KU specimen, 1965, locality "NO LOCALITY", no state: it names only the country. COL says Africa, but a kept animal can't be told from a free one here. Too thin to call, so it stays.
MNHN specimen, no year, locality Bangui. The NTNU record says only "Africa continent" (10,000 km), so it adds nothing. COL says Africa, but one undated town record doesn't settle a free animal.
Locality "Zoologischer Garten Frankfurt am Main": a zoo, NABU|naturgucker record of a captive animal. No other counted record here.

Two undated MNHN (Paris) specimens with no locality, at one point 0.1 km from Paris Zoological Park (Wikidata Q1969385). COL says Africa. Points to zoo animals, but the records themselves don't name one.
iNaturalist research-grade record, Machinga, 2023, and NABU|naturgucker, Majete Wildlife Reserve, 2025: two datasets, no captive mark. COL says Africa.
ROM specimen, no year, field locality Vola, Upper Benue River, no captive sign. COL says Africa.
iNaturalist research-grade record, Eastern Province, 2023, coordinates to 31 km, no captive mark. COL says Africa.

245 records: 179 Borror Lab sound recordings, all 20 we read in zoo pens and yards (Columbus, Pittsburgh, Potter Park, Brookfield); 64 iBOL sequences and 2 specimens unread. No captive field filled, and COL says Africa. The rest is inferred, not stated.
Angelo State specimen, locality "San Antonio Zoo", a taxidermy head. The record itself names the zoo; no other counted record here.

All 390 are EEZA (CSIC, Almería) specimens in one ungulate collection, 1971–2008; all 20 we read say "Almería; Finca La Hoya", one farm address. COL says Africa. Points to a herd kept at the institute, but no record says captive, and 370 are unread.
MHNG specimen, no year or locality, coordinates to 1,000 km: it names only the country. COL says Africa, which can't show a free animal in Ethiopia. Too thin to call, so it stays.
CAS specimen, 1930, field locality Loita, no captive sign. COL says only Africa, one old specimen is all there is, and nothing on it says how it was told from other gazelles. So it doesn't settle it.
CIBIO field record, 2012, Termit, Loulou Kiraman, 100 m uncertainty, found dead; no captive sign. COL says Africa.

AMNH specimen, 1938, no locality, establishmentMeans "native", coordinates 5.98, -79.80 at sea south of Panama. A land animal at sea is misplaced or misidentified, and COL says Africa, but the record doesn't say so. Same pattern as 50:MX.

iNaturalist research-grade record, Saint-Louis, 2008; its remark says the animals were reintroduced to the reserve. Introduced counts as keep, though a reserve may be fenced. The only record, and COL says only Africa.

LACM specimen, no year, locality Fada, a town, coordinates to 90 km, establishmentMeans native, no captive sign. COL says Africa, but a town and no date don't show where the animal lived. GBIF now returns 1 record, the snapshot 2.
Seven specimens, and each names a zoo: Oakland (2), Honolulu (2), Hogle, San Antonio, Houston. The records themselves name the zoos, and they're every counted record here.
FMNH specimen, 1949, Rio Nain on the upper Rio Sinu, and a Corantioquia fauna inventory record, Antioquia: two datasets, no captive sign.
Two records, each naming a captive site: Borror Lab recording "Interior pens, Columbus Zoo" and CAS skull "San Francisco Zoo". They're every counted record here.
Locality "Zoologischer Garten Frankfurt am Main": a zoo, NABU|naturgucker record of a captive animal. No other counted record here.

An Ibaraki Nature Museum specimen, Kumamoto, 1998, no locality, and an iBOL record "Mined from GenBank", coordinates near the middle of Japan. Neither documents a free animal, and COL says South America. Inferred from the record types, not stated.
LACM specimen, 1939, Caledonia Bay, establishmentMeans native, no captive sign. COL lists only South America, so no second source agrees for Panama.
Two Conservation International RAP survey records, 1992 and 1996, Pampas del Heath and Aguas Clara Camp: field surveys, no captive sign. COL lists South America.
Machine-observation record, Paso Centurión, Cerro Largo, 2013, 10 m uncertainty, from a local mammal survey, no captive sign. COL lists South America.

iNaturalist research-grade record, Sipaliwini, 2018, coordinates to 31 km, no captive mark. A community-verified observation, but the only record here, and the species has no COL id, so no second source agrees.

Two ROM specimens, no year, locality "Colony at Ottawa": the word points to a kept laboratory colony, but neither record says captive or names a keeper. They're every counted record here. COL says Middle America.

Two NABU|naturgucker records: "Luisenpark - Mannheim", 2018, a park that keeps animals, and a former military site in Berlin, 2015, a field locality with no captive mark: likely a released animal. One dataset, and COL says Middle America, so no second source agrees.

Two Auckland Museum specimens, 1980, no locality, coordinates with 800 km uncertainty, so they name only the country. A kept animal can't be told from a free one here, and COL says Middle America. Too thin to call, so it stays.

iBOL record "Mined from GenBank": a sequence, no locality, no date, coordinates near the middle of Ukraine. It documents no animal there, and COL says Middle America. Inferred from the record type, not stated by it.
